purpose: IOTA ML is a project-based visual machine-learning application. Users create projects, upload CSV datasets, create workflows, connect scientific nodes, configure nodes, execute workflows, inspect outputs, and pin selected outputs to analysis boards.

topics.title: Projects
topics.summary: Projects are the top-level containers for datasets and saved workflows.
details: The Projects page separates projects owned by the user from projects the user can access.
Project cards show access level, state, priority, owner/assignment information, workflow count, dataset count, and last update.
Users with permission can create a new project from the Projects page.

topics.title: Creating a project
topics.summary: Project creation is organized around project information, project data, and workflows.
details: First create the project and save its basic information.
Then upload project datasets.
Then create at least one workflow and open it in the workspace.

topics.title: Project datasets
topics.summary: Project datasets are CSV files stored inside a project and made available to workflows in that project.
details: The current project uploader accepts CSV files.
Dataset information includes row count, column count, storage size, creation date, and column metadata.
Column metadata includes column name, data type, missing count, and unique count.

topics.title: Workflows
topics.summary: A workflow is a saved visual graph of connected nodes inside a project.
details: Each workflow belongs to a project and keeps its own graph and execution history.
Users build workflows by adding nodes and connecting compatible ports.
A workflow can be executed as a whole, or the selected node can be run together with the upstream nodes required for it.

topics.title: Workflow workspace
topics.summary: The workspace is the visual editor used to build, configure, run, inspect, and version workflows.
details: The workspace contains the node palette, workflow canvas, top toolbar, and right-side panel.
The top toolbar includes workflow execution, Analysis Board access, named version saving, auto-layout, workflow export, and project navigation.
The right-side panel contains node outputs, node settings, run history, the AI assistant, workflow versions, and reusable components.

topics.title: Node palette
topics.summary: The node palette is the searchable catalog used to add available scientific nodes to a workflow.
details: Nodes are grouped by category.
The palette can be searched by node name, category, or description.
Node definitions used by the AI assistant come from the live backend node registry, not from this guide.

topics.title: Node settings
topics.summary: Selecting a node exposes its configurable parameters and available inputs/outputs.
details: Node configuration is edited in the node settings area or node dialog.
The exact settings, defaults, ports, and validation rules differ by node.
For exact node settings, the AI assistant must query the live node registry before answering.

topics.title: Workflow execution
topics.summary: Workflows and selected nodes can be executed from the workspace.
details: Running the whole workflow executes the workflow graph according to its dependencies.
When a node is selected, the run control can execute that node together with the upstream nodes required for it.
Run history is available in the right-side panel and supports inspecting previous runs.

topics.title: Node results
topics.summary: Execution outputs are inspected from the Results area in the workspace.
details: Results can include tables, charts, and other node-specific output types.
The Results panel is tied to workflow execution results.
Supported outputs can be pinned from the Results panel to an Analysis Board.

topics.title: Analysis Board
topics.summary: Analysis Boards are used to collect and arrange selected workflow outputs for analysis and presentation.
details: Outputs are added to a board from the Results panel.
The main board is always available and additional board tabs can be used when supported by the workflow.
Board items represent persisted workflow outputs rather than new executions.

topics.title: Workflow versions
topics.summary: Named workflow versions preserve workflow states that can later be inspected or restored.
details: A named version can be saved from the workflow toolbar.
Versions are managed from the Workflow Versions tab in the right-side panel.
Version preview is read-only until the user returns to the current version or restores a selected version.

topics.title: Reusable workflow components
topics.summary: Selected workflow nodes can be grouped into reusable components.
details: The workspace can convert selected nodes into a component when the selection is valid.
Components are managed from the Components tab in the right-side panel.
Component management includes versioning, export/import, archive, edit, and delete operations where permitted.

topics.title: IOTA AI assistant
topics.summary: The IOTA AI assistant is a read-only guide for app usage, node knowledge, workflow design, and current-workflow inspection.
details: The assistant should answer app-usage questions using the app guide.
It should answer exact node questions using the live node registry.
It may inspect the current workflow when the user asks about that workflow.
In the current phase it must not create, modify, save, or execute workflows.
